links.comparator_used: Pre-deployment baseline COMPOSER BPA without LLM augmentation (counterfactual estimated by Bayesian structural time-series from pre-deployment trends)
links.outcome: Proportion of sepsis BPAs acknowledged by nurses as "No Infection Suspected" (proxy for clinical acceptance); time to antibiotics as a safety check
links.effect: Model-predicted rate would have stayed around 25-30% without LLM; observed rate dropped approximately 18-22%, with pointwise deviations of roughly -5% to -15% and cumulative difference about -90% to -100%. Median BPA-to-antibiotics time went from 140.4 to 112.1 minutes. 2539 pre and 1978 post BPA events.
links.tradeoff: "Will notify MD immediately" acknowledgements also fell, which the authors attribute to nurses using it interchangeably with "Sepsis Treatment/Workup in Progress". Median alert-to-initial-workup time rose from 104.1 to 132.3 minutes. 45% of nurses still agreed the BPA often identifies patients without infection. Authors note LLM infrastructure costs and a quasi-experimental design that cannot establish causality.
links.quote: The causal impact analysis demonstrated a significant reduction in the percentage of BPAs acknowledged as “No Infection Suspected” following the deployment of COMPOSER-LLM.

design_hint: LLM note-based augmentation of an existing sepsis alert to reduce false alerts
